intent: Put every dependency this repo declares on its newest stable release, and install the shared dependency-freshness gate so it stays there.
scope: Non-goal: no source changes; this is manifests and gate wiring only
changes: Exact-pinned 95 previously range-specified dependencies to their newest stable release, via ~/.claude/scripts/apply_dep_pins.py driven by the gate's own --json findings.
Moved the gatelock git-tag dependency from gatelock-v0.1.0 to gatelock-v0.7.2 -- six minor versions of drift that a PEP 508 direct reference hid from every previous check.
Installed the shared gate's three pieces (delegate, pre-commit hook, CI workflow) from ~/utils/dep_freshness/templates.

verification.evidence: exit 0; clean venv rebuilt from the repinned meta/requirements.txt, pre-commit --all-files and the full suite green inside it

risks: gatelock v0.1.0 -> v0.7.2 is a six-version jump in a shared library; the clean-venv mirror is what exercises it here.
Exact pins mean CI goes red on any upstream release until the pin is bumped. That is the chosen behaviour, not a regression.
rollback: git revert the commit; the pins and the three gate files are the whole change.
After reverting, re-run ci_mirror.sh to confirm the older pins still resolve.
